events.title: Mongol sack of Kyiv
hints: After a siege in December 1240 a great medieval capital on the Dnieper was destroyed.
A hill fortress fell after days of bombardment by siege engines.
events.summary: Batu Khan's Mongol army besieged Kyiv in the winter of 1240 and took the city on 6 December after heavy bombardment. The sack devastated the former capital of Rus', and a large part of the population was killed or enslaved.

events.title: Crimean slave raids
hints: Mounted raiders from the south drove captives across the steppe to a Black Sea port.
The market at Kaffa in the Crimea was one of the largest slave markets in Europe.
events.summary: From the 15th to the 18th century, Tatar horsemen of the Crimean Khanate raided the Ukrainian, Russian and Polish lands, carrying captives to be sold at slave markets such as Kaffa. Estimates of the number taken run into the millions over several centuries.
events.wikipediaTitle: Crimean–Nogai slave raids in Eastern Europe

events.title: Union of Lublin and Polish rule
hints: A union in 1569 moved the central lands from a grand duchy to the crown of a neighbouring kingdom.
Great estates grew rich on grain exported down the Vistula.
events.summary: In 1569 the Union of Lublin transferred Volhynia, Podolia, Bratslav and Kyiv from the Grand Duchy of Lithuania to the Polish crown. Magnates acquired huge estates worked by serfs, and the grain trade and religious and social tension contributed to the Cossack uprising of 1648.

events.title: Habsburg Galicia
territoryNames: the Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria
hints: A first partition of a neighbouring kingdom in 1772 created a new Habsburg crown land.
The province became known as one of the poorest in the empire.
events.summary: In the First Partition of Poland in 1772 Austria acquired the Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria, including Lviv. It was known as one of the poorest provinces of the empire, with a state salt monopoly, and was lost at the end of the First World War.

events.title: Valuev Circular and Ems Ukaz
hints: An 1863 circular declared that a language spoken by millions had never existed.
An 1876 decree banned publishing and stage performances in it.
events.summary: The 1863 Valuev Circular restricted publishing in Ukrainian, claiming there had never been a separate 'Little Russian' language. The Ems Ukaz of 1876 further banned printing, theatre and music in the language, and the bans were relaxed only after the 1905 revolution.
events.quip: An official declaration that a language of millions did not exist.

events.title: Soviet invasion in the Ukrainian–Soviet War
hints: A new government in Petrograd sent an expeditionary force south within weeks of seizing power.
A republic with its capital at Kyiv was overrun several times between 1917 and 1920.
Soviet rule was secured in 1921 after years of war with several rival armies.
events.summary: After the October Revolution the Bolsheviks sent forces under Vladimir Antonov-Ovseyenko into Ukraine in December 1917 and took Kyiv in January 1918. Fighting with the Ukrainian People's Republic and other armies continued until 1921. Modern Ukrainian historians regard it as a failed war of independence.

events.title: Occupation by the Central Powers
hints: After the 'bread peace' of February 1918 foreign troops moved in to collect food.
A hetman installed with foreign backing ruled until November 1918.
events.summary: After the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk with the Ukrainian People's Republic in February 1918, German and Austro-Hungarian troops occupied the country to secure grain deliveries. In April 1918 Germany backed a coup that installed Hetman Pavlo Skoropadskyi until the end of the war.

events.title: Holodomor
hints: Grain quotas, blacklisted villages and sealed borders turned a bad harvest into a catastrophe.
Many countries now recognise it as a genocide, though historians debate the intent.
events.summary: In 1932–33 Soviet grain procurement quotas, the blacklisting of villages and restrictions on movement led to a famine in the Ukrainian SSR that killed an estimated 3.5 to 5 million people. Ukraine and many other countries recognise it as a genocide, while historians continue to debate its intent.

events.title: Soviet invasion of eastern Poland and annexation of the west
hints: An army crossed a border on 17 September 1939 under a secret deal with another dictator.
Lviv was occupied within days.
Staged elections led to annexation into a Soviet republic in November 1939.
events.summary: On 17 September 1939 the Red Army invaded eastern Poland under the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact and took Eastern Galicia and Volhynia, including Lviv. After staged elections the territory was incorporated into the Ukrainian SSR in November 1939.
events.wikipediaTitle: Soviet annexation of Eastern Galicia and Volhynia

events.title: Nazi German occupation
hints: A civil administration split the country into districts, with a capital at Rivne.
In late September 1941 about 34,000 Jews were shot in a ravine outside Kyiv.
events.summary: German forces occupied the country from 1941 and ruled most of it through the Reichskommissariat Ukraine, extracting grain and deporting several million people as forced labourers. Mass killings of Jews and others included Babi Yar in September 1941.

events.title: Annexation of Crimea
hints: Unmarked troops took control of the peninsula's parliament in February 2014.
A UN General Assembly resolution affirmed the country's territorial integrity.
events.summary: In February and March 2014 Russian forces took control of Crimea and, after a referendum not recognised internationally, Russia declared it annexed. UN General Assembly Resolution 68/262 affirmed Ukraine's territorial integrity, and most states do not recognise the annexation.
events.wikipediaTitle: Annexation of Crimea by the Russian Federation

events.title: War in Donbas and Russian military involvement
hints: Armed groups seized government buildings in the east in April 2014.
A passenger airliner was shot down over the region in July 2014.
The war lasted until it was absorbed into a full-scale invasion in February 2022.
events.summary: From April 2014 Russian-backed armed groups seized territory in the Donbas and declared the Donetsk and Luhansk 'people's republics'. Russia denied sending troops, but its military was covertly and directly involved and the separatist entities were largely under Russian control. The war ended when it was absorbed by the 2022 invasion.

events.title: Full-scale Russian invasion
hints: A large-scale offensive from three directions began on 24 February 2022.
The UN General Assembly demanded a withdrawal in March 2022.
events.summary: Russia launched a full-scale invasion on 24 February 2022 and occupied parts of the south and east. The UN General Assembly demanded its withdrawal, and the war has caused large numbers of civilian deaths and millions of refugees.
